hook: Builders now pay *₹3,000* a tanker, three times borewell water
hook_b: Builders now pay *₹3,000* a tanker, three times borewell water
tldr: With fresh borewell permissions restricted as groundwater falls, construction sites in Hyderabad are buying private tanker water at about ₹3,000 a load against ₹1,000 earlier.

beats.what: Sites that used borewells now rely on private tankers; a 5-7 floor building spends ₹25,000-30,000 a month on water, per the Cyberabad Builders Association.
beats.why: Falling groundwater, curbs on new borewells and the El Niño threat, builders say.
beats.care: Builders estimate about 350-400 ongoing projects are hit, and handovers could be delayed.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: Builders say it could worsen from December, when reservoir levels are expected to come under more pressure.

cards.q: Who should carry the extra water cost?

facts.t: Projects of 500+ units could need *10-15* tankers a day without groundwater, per the Telangana Builders Federation.

viz.l: Water cost per load for a construction site
viz.verdict: Builders pay more; buyers may face delays

insight: Builders estimate water has added about ₹10 per sq ft to construction costs.
watch: December reservoir levels, which builders say could slow construction further.

sources.name: Times of India
sources.title: El Niño threat puts construction sector in Hyderabad under water stress; builders pay three times more for water

fact: Hyderabad builders now pay *₹3,000* a water tanker, three times borewell cost
twist: Builders fear flats due by mid-2027 could slip by up to *six months*, into late 2027 or 2028.
